title: Python Project Packaging, Modules and Entry Points
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and behaviour of Python Project Packaging, Modules and Entry Points.
Choose an appropriate python project packaging, modules and entry points technique for an application.
Interpret representative code and output involving python project packaging, modules and entry points.
Identify limitations and failure modes for python project packaging, modules and entry points.
Apply the concepts in maintainable Python code.

understand.concept: A Python project should separate importable application code from command-line startup, tests and project metadata. Packages organize modules into a stable namespace. A pyproject.toml file describes build-system and project metadata for modern packaging workflows. A console script entry point exposes a command that invokes a Python function after installation.
understand.whyItMatters: Consistent project structure makes applications easier to install, test, reuse and distribute.
understand.analogy: A package is a well-organized toolbox with labels and an instruction card explaining how to use it.
understand.analogyLimit: A directory layout and metadata do not guarantee good API design, dependency safety or compatibility across platforms.
understand.summary: Python Project Packaging, Modules and Entry Points develops practical application engineering skills for Python projects.

explain.narrative:
## Organize code for reuse and distribution
Keep application logic in importable modules and put command-line parsing in a thin entry point. Use `pyproject.toml` for project metadata and build configuration. A `src/` layout can prevent accidental imports from the repository root during tests. Define dependencies explicitly, choose a supported Python range and build artifacts in a clean environment. Do not execute application work merely because a module is imported; protect startup with a main guard.
